MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Service

PATIENT DETAILS
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood (EDTA)
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Testing for Autosomal Dominant Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia (AD-HSP)

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Index patient referred for genetic testing for hereditary spastic paraplegia.

METHODOLOGY
Direct sequencing for SPAST gene point mutations:
- Entire SPAST coding region including intron-exon boundaries screened
- Fluorescent DNA sequencing methodology employed
- Detection rate >98% for point mutations

MLPA analysis for copy number variants:
- GeneScan MLPA kit X165 utilized
- All SPAST exons tested
- 13/14 coding exons of SPG3a gene tested
- Analysis for exon deletions and duplications

RESULTS

SPAST gene analysis (NM_014946.3):
Sequence variant detected: c.1536G>T (p.Glu512Asp)
Location: Exon 13
Zygosity: Heterozygous
Classification: Pathogenic

SPG3a gene analysis:
No pathogenic variants detected
No copy number variants detected

Bioinformatics Analysis:
- In silico prediction tools indicate damaging effect
- Variant previously reported in affected individuals with HSP
- Absent from population databases
- Located in functionally important AAA ATPase domain

SUMMARY
A heterozygous pathogenic variant c.1536G>T (p.Glu512Asp) has been detected in exon 13 of the SPAST gene. This result is consistent with the clinical diagnosis of hereditary spastic paraplegia. The detected variant has been previously reported in multiple affected individuals and is predicted to be pathogenic by bioinformatics analysis.

SPAST mutations are the most common cause of autosomal dominant HSP, accounting for approximately 40% of AD-HSP cases. Combined with SPG3a mutations, these two genes account for ~50% of all AD-HSP cases.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss inheritance pattern and recurrence risks
2. Cascade testing is available for at-risk family members
3. Prenatal testing is available for this variant
4. Presymptomatic testing should be undertaken with appropriate genetic counseling

METHODOLOGICAL NOTES
This test detects point mutations and small insertions/deletions in the SPAST gene with >98% sensitivity. Large deletions/duplications are detected by MLPA analysis. Rare variants in non-coding regions or deep intronic variants may not be detected by this methodology.

REFERENCES
1. Hazan J et al. (1999) Spastin, a new AAA protein, is altered in the most frequent form of autosomal dominant spastic paraplegia. Nat Genet 23:296-303
2. Solowska JM & Baas PW (2015) Hereditary spastic paraplegia SPG4: what is known and not known about the disease. Brain 138:2471-2484

Authorized by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Report checked by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
